newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banco Noroeste jumps after sale announced.
newsitem.headline: Banco Noroeste jumps after sale announced.

text.p: Preferred stock of Brazilian private bank Banco Noroeste jumped 9.4 percent to 1.63 reais following news that a controlling stake would be sold to a leading Spanish bank, brokers said.
Trading in the stock had been delayed until 1300 local/1600 GMT because of the announcement of the deal.
Banco Santander SA on Friday said its Brazilian unit Banco Geral do Comercio would buy a 50-percent controlling stake in Noroeste for an estimated $500 million.
Only five trades were made on Noroeste preferred, worth 19,000 reais, traders said. No trades have been made on the bank's common stock so far.
The deal, which has to be approved by Brazilian authorities, puts an end to months of speculation that Noroeste was due to be sold to Santander.
Noroeste is a medium-sized bank, focusing on retail investors and small and medium corporate clients.
In the first half, the bank posted a net profit of 42.8 million reais, up from 29 million reais in the same period last year.
